title: Timestral

primary_sources.paraphrase: Model card of the 209M checkpoint, largest of four sizes. Zero-shot probabilistic forecasts (21 quantiles), past-only and known-future covariates, context up to 32,768 steps, runs on CPU. Lists vendor-reported GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench scores against Chronos-2, t0-gamma, TimesFM-3 and Toto-2.0. Training data not stated.

Tech report (v1, 2026-10-27). Says the family sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench, with the 209M and 123M models in the top two places on every metric. Known-future covariates are native. Pretrained on synthetic data, post-trained on unnamed real plus synthetic data.

Release post (2026-10-15). Says the 209M model ranks first among pretrained zero-shot models on the three benchmarks with a single checkpoint, and that a one-day-ahead forecast takes 113 ms on an 8-thread server CPU. No electricity-load example.

Inference code under Apache 2.0, one commit, no tags. forecast() accepts known_covariates covering context plus horizon, and past_covariates. No benchmark reproduction scripts described in the README.
File listing of the weights repository: model.safetensors was last changed in commit 7394bc19c4b48dfb9c0872689eed058d3216331a on 2026-10-15; the head of main (9874d252) changed only the README.

Modified MIT licence over the weights: MIT-style grant with attribution, withdrawn for organisations whose global monthly revenue exceeded 20 million USD in the preceding month unless they obtain a commercial licence from Mistral.

Full text of the report. No named real training datasets, no statement on overlap with benchmark test sets, no with/without-covariate comparison, no energy-specific breakdown. IND-Eval (energy, manufacturing, transport) is reported in aggregate only.

claims.text: The 209M and 123M models take the top two places on every metric of GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among zero-shot models.
claims.baseline: other pretrained zero-shot models on the leaderboards

claims.text: Timestral-209M scores MASE 0.658 on GIFT-Eval; Chronos-2 scores 0.698.
Timestral-209M scores CRPS 0.446 on GIFT-Eval; Chronos-2 scores 0.485.
Timestral-209M scores MASE 0.626 on TIME; Chronos-2 scores 0.662.
Timestral-209M scores CRPS 0.522 on TIME; Chronos-2 scores 0.556.
Timestral-209M reaches an SQL skill score of 50.39 on fev-bench; Chronos-2 reaches 47.28.
Timestral-209M reaches a MASE skill score of 39.49 on fev-bench; Chronos-2 reaches 35.50.
On IND-Eval (energy, manufacturing, transport; aggregate only) Timestral-209M scores a normalised MASE of 0.646.
On IND-Eval Timestral-209M scores a normalised CRPS of 0.435.
A one-day-ahead forecast from three weeks of 15-minute history takes 113 ms with the 209M model on an 8-thread server CPU; no GPU is needed.
The models accept known-future covariates natively, passed to forecast() alongside the target history.

relevance.rationale: A general-purpose forecasting model: its evidence is on mixed-domain benchmarks, with no hourly electric-load result (target 1). The benchmark horizons were not found in the sources read; the only stated example is one day ahead at 15-minute steps, and the model can emit 1,024 steps in one pass, which covers our 168 hours (horizon 1). It takes numeric known-future covariates, so temperature can be supplied as our spec requires, although no source tests it with weather (covariates 3, on capability).

checks.notes: pre_registered: no; the sources are a vendor release post, model card and tech report, none describing a plan fixed before the results. training_overlap_risk: the weights file model.safetensors was committed on 2026-10-15 (commit 7394bc19, read from the Hugging Face file listing); of the 52 scored weeks (2025-11-10 to 2026-11-02) only 3 start after that date (2026-10-19, 10-26, 11-02), fewer than half, so high. The report does not name its real post-training data or a data cutoff, so whether PJM or EIA load is in it could not be verified. independent_replication: unknown; two searches found no independent result on electricity load and no leakage audit. One article said to rerun the 209M model on GIFT-Eval could not be fetched (HTTP 403) and is not counted; a third-party leaderboard listing and commentary pages surfaced by search were not opened. evidence_strength: moderate; the numbers are public and tied to open weights and code and to public leaderboards, but they are vendor-reported, not pre-registered, the test-window length was not found, and whether the compared models received the same covariates is not stated. No interval is given for any number. Not verified: the leaderboard ranks themselves (leaderboard pages not opened), the CPU latency on our laptop, the 60-minute runtime limit for 52 windows, and the date of the GitHub commit. Licence: Modified MIT with a revenue cap of 20 million USD per month; commercial use is conditional, so license_ok_for_commercial is left null and flagged here.

license: Modified MIT (Mistral; rights withdrawn above 20 million USD monthly revenue without a commercial licence)
label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: A covariate-aware model release with open weights, code, a model card and a tech report, and it is already listed as runnable with temperature in our spec. Its published evidence is general-benchmark only and its weights date leaves 3 of 52 scored weeks after it, so the run must carry that label.
implementation_hint: Run models_ff/run_ff.py with mistralai/Timestral-209M (ff_native_exog, temperature as known-future covariate), pinned at revision 9874d252ab0aae16f7f7c999f98f98d6ad7d8365 (weights file from commit 7394bc19c4b48dfb9c0872689eed058d3216331a, 2026-10-15). Report n_windows_after_weights = 3. Smaller checkpoints (123M, 28M, 5M) exist if CPU runtime is a problem.

receipt.claimed: On general benchmarks the release reports Timestral-209M ahead of Chronos-2 among zero-shot models (for example MASE 0.658 against 0.698 on GIFT-Eval).
receipt.horizon_mismatch: The claim is about general multi-domain benchmarks against other pretrained models; ours is hourly load on two PJM zones, a week ahead, with temperature, against a regression with temperature. Only 1 of the 48 scored weeks starts after the weights were published.
